title: Deferred-prefill with kernel-affinity micro-slices to balance latency and throughput
creator: Ethan Cole
description:
Problem: Our current prefill/decode scheduler optimizes for either latency-heavy workloads (by hedging and early dispatch) or throughput-heavy workloads (by aggressive batching), but struggles when the workload mix requires both low tail latency and kernel-level efficiency. Kernel selection changes (quantization, fused-kernels, attention layout) make some requests much cheaper when grouped, yet naive grouping introduces head-of-line latency for small interactive requests.

Proposal summary: Implement a 'deferred-prefill' scheduling mode combined with kernel-affinity micro-slicing. The scheduler briefly defers dispatch of newly-arrived prefill requests (configurable micro-window: 4-12ms) to opportunistically coalesce requests into small micro-slices that maximize kernel reuse (same model variant, quantization profile, attention layout) while bounding added latency. Micro-slices are constrained by an SLO-aware deadline: if the linger window would violate a request's latency budget, the request takes a fast-path immediate dispatch. We introduce kernel-affinity tags and a lightweight cost model to decide when to hold vs dispatch.

Why different: Instead of large batching windows which harm latency, micro-slices aim for the Pareto point where kernel warmup and fused attention kernels realize most of their speedup with only a few combined requests. Deferred-prefill puts the decision at the scheduler layer based on kernel affinity and per-request deadlines rather than at the runtime kernel layer alone.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler implements a configurable micro-window (default 8ms) and kernel-affinity tagging for requests.
Lab A/B experiments show >=18% token-cost reduction for mixed workloads with <=5% increase in P95 latency compared to baseline immediate dispatch.
P99 latency for interactive tier remains within SLOs when micro-slicing is enabled with conservative config.
Canary rollout plan exists and a runtime flag allows safe rollback to current behavior.
Unit + integration tests cover affinity matching, deadline preemption, and fast-path execution.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature-flag behind runtime-scheduler flag and traffic-limited canary (5% of teams, low-risk models) for 48h. Monitor P50/P95/P99 latency, token cost, kernel selection distribution, and rejection/fallback rates. Phase 2: expand to 25% with more diverse models and sequence lengths for 7 days. Phase 3: enable by default for mixed tier with conservative defaults, and expose micro-window config in Dedicated/Private consoles. Rollback: flip runtime flag to disable hold-window immediately (fast-path existing code).
technical_notes: Affinity tagging: compute 8-bit affinity hash from (model-id, quantization-profile, attention-layout, seqlen-bucket). Keep tags in request metadata for scheduler decisions.
Cost model: maintain EWMA of per-token GPU time per affinity bucket plus estimated kernel-warmup cost. Use this to compute expected cost-savings from coalescing two or more requests.

Deadline check: each request carries an effective latency budget (from route SLO or client tier). Scheduler computes hold_deadline = arrival_ts + micro_window; if hold_deadline > request_deadline then mark immediate=true.

Micro-slice formation: within micro-window, group requests by exact affinity tag. If group reaches size N_opt (empirical, usually 2-6) or micro-window expires, create micro-slice job. Otherwise, dispatch remaining requests via fast-path.
Fast-path: immediate dispatch bypassing hold-window to preserve latency for P0/P1 requests or when affinity mismatch prevents beneficial coalescing.

Fairness: implement per-customer token-buckets and weighted queueing. If a single tenant's requests are consistently occupying micro-slices and causing starvation, apply proportional backpressure and enforce per-tenant cap per micro-window.
Integration with kernel selector: micro-slice carries preferred kernel selection hints; runtime still validates/chooses final kernel for hardware and model compatibility.
Observability: expose metrics: micro_slices_created, average_slice_size, micro_window_wait_ms, kernelaffinity_hit_rate, cost_savings_estimate, fallback_rate, per-tenant-starvation_flag.
Edge cases: streaming requests with interleaved prefill/decode cycles use separate affinity windows per phase to avoid mixing decode kernels with prefill kernels.
experiments: AB test A: Mixed chat workload (70% short interactive, 30% high-throughput embedder) vs baseline immediate dispatch. Measure cost/token and P95 latency over 72h.
AB test B: Vary micro-window {4ms,8ms,12ms} across cohorts to find knee for different cluster sizes and inter-arrival distributions.
Kernel-probe run: intentionally route small groups to fused-attn kernels to measure real-world warmup gains and verify scheduler's cost model predictions.
Fairness sweep: simulate heavy single-tenant load and validate per-tenant caps and starvation metrics under 95th percentile loads.
